Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion

Class PoseSourceConfig

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.PoseSourceConfig
public class PoseSourceConfig extends Object
Filter thresholds for a PoseSource.

Fluent setters, like the rest of the feature's configuration objects: 


 var config = PoseSourceConfig.forAprilTags()
         .withMaxAngularVelocity(DegreesPerSecond.of(540))
         .withMaxAmbiguity(0.25);

How a filter is switched off

Every threshold starts at infinity, which is the way of saying "no limit": the comparison value <= INFINITY always passes, so an unconfigured filter filters nothing. There are no enable flags or sentinel values to memorise.

    • forAprilTags

      public static PoseSourceConfig forAprilTags()
      A sensible preset for a camera looking at AprilTags.

      The numbers are defensible starting points, not truths: 720 degrees per second is roughly where motion blur starts to ruin PnP on a global-shutter camera, and an ambiguity of 0.3 is the threshold PhotonVision recommends. Tune them against your own data.

      Returns:
      a new configuration.

    • forVisualInertialOdometry

      public static PoseSourceConfig forVisualInertialOdometry()
      A sensible preset for a visual-inertial odometry source such as QuestNav.

      No angular velocity limit: a VIO does not do PnP, so turning does not affect it the way it affects a camera. No ambiguity, because it reports none. The Mahalanobis gate is tighter because a VIO should not jump, and when it does --- re-acquisition after losing tracking --- that is exactly what needs catching.

      Returns:
      a new configuration.

    • withMahalanobisGate

      public PoseSourceConfig withMahalanobisGate(double sigmas, double baseStdDevMeters, double baseStdDevRadians, double driftVariancePerSecond)
      Configures the Mahalanobis filter, which discards measurements too far from what the estimator already believes.

      The uncertainty it compares against grows with time since the last accepted measurement. That is what makes the filter useful rather than a padlock: if a source has contributed nothing for ten seconds, the estimator may have wandered off, and the filter opens up to let it be corrected.

      Parameters:
      sigmas - maximum distance in sigmas. 3 is tight, 5 is permissive.
      baseStdDevMeters - position uncertainty of a freshly corrected estimator.
      baseStdDevRadians - heading uncertainty of a freshly corrected estimator.
      driftVariancePerSecond - how much variance the odometry adds per second without a correction.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.
